note: Every normative rule in ADR 0001 maps to at least one probe. A 'static' probe is a shell command run from the repo root and passes on exit 0. A 'live' probe is a message sent through the real daemon delivery path and read back with tg_get_messages; its observation is recorded in live-evidence.json and re-validated here, so the runner checks the recorded observation rather than trusting a claim. A 'ci' probe reads a GitHub Actions conclusion. Run: python3 docs/adr/probes/run.py

probes.claim: a local image reference is claimed by the image family and rendered inline as a photo entry
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'pub(crate) fn is_supported_image' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF '![{alt}](tg://photo?id={id}{title})' src/utils/image.rs

probes.claim: the image kind is decided by the head BYTES (PNG/JPEG/GIF87a/GIF89a/RIFF-WEBP/BMP signatures), not by the file extension
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'b"\xff\xd8\xff"' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'GIF89a' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'WEBP' src/utils/image.rs

probes.claim: a local video reference is claimed by the video family via an ISO-BMFF box walk and rendered as a video entry
every other file kind gets a document media entry with a recorded ResolvedFileRef
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'pub const DOC_ID_PREFIX' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'self.entries.push(ResolvedFileRef' src/utils/image.rs

claim: the .md exception is gone from the CONFIG and the CODE; the only surviving mentions are comments and the test that asserts its absence

probes.claim: with no rich path every kind still ships as its own detached bubble
a document reference is emitted in LINK syntax and never in image syntax
a photo and a video reference are emitted in image syntax, because that is what the client renders for a media block
the walk reads both markdown forms, so the form the author typed does not decide the route
a reference the media array cannot answer is neutralised before the send, never left to 400 the message
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'pub(crate) fn neutralize_orphan_photo_refs' src/channels/telegram/rich/mermaid.rs && grep -qF 'neutralize_orphan_photo_refs' src/channels/telegram/rich/api.rs

probes.claim: a media entry Telegram refuses costs that entry, not the whole rich plane
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'fn retry_rich_media_around_offender' src/channels/telegram/rich/api.rs && grep -qF 'fn is_media_entry_rejection' src/channels/telegram/rich/api.rs

probes.claim: the final leg suppresses itself when a recorded intermediate already carries the same reply, comparing reference spelling rather than whitespace
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'normalize_reference_spelling' src/channels/telegram/delivery.rs && grep -qF 'pub(crate) fn normalize_reference_spelling' src/channels/telegram/intermediates.rs

probes.claim: the three media families namespace their ids (`img`/`vid`/`doc`) so a reference can only ever be answered by an entry of its own kind — the property that lets one message carry mixed kinds
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'pub const IMG_ID_PREFIX: &str = "img";' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'pub const VID_ID_PREFIX: &str = "vid";' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'pub const DOC_ID_PREFIX: &str = "doc";' src/utils/image.rs

probes.claim: a caption rides the markdown title, and a caption that cannot be expressed with the one measured delimiter is DROPPED rather than emitted malformed (the image still arrives, merely unnamed)
dedup compares the RESOLVED ABSOLUTE path in all three families (image, video, file), so two spellings of one file (`~/x.png` and `/root/x.png`) cannot ship twice

the photo/document split is a property of the byte length: at or below the 10 MiB `sendPhoto` ceiling the image ships as a photo, above it as a document, so an un-previewable picture beats a missing one. ONE constant serves both planes -- the tool floor (send.rs) and the rich rewriter (utils/image.rs) -- so they cannot drift apart
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'pub const TELEGRAM_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 10 * 1024 * 1024;' src/utils/image.rs && grep -qF 'pub use crate::utils::image::TELEGRAM_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES;' src/channels/telegram/send.rs && grep -qF 'if len <= TELEGRAM_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES {' src/channels/telegram/send.rs && grep -qF '.map(|meta| meta.len() > TELEGRAM_PHOTO_MAX_BYTES)' src/utils/image.rs
probes.claim_revised: 2026-11-14 (#823 L16): the constant moved to utils::image and is re-exported by send.rs, because the rich rewriter lives outside the `telegram` feature gate and could not import it. The old cmd pinned the definition inside send.rs, which the move legitimately falsified.

probes.claim: a video ships as `sendVideo` only when it is MPEG-4 within the 50 MiB ceiling; anything else falls to `sendDocument`, which has no container gate and therefore cannot silently drop the file
probes.cmd: grep -qF 'if len <= TELEGRAM_VIDEO_MAX_BYTES && format == VideoFormat::Mpeg4' src/channels/telegram/send.rs

probes.claim: `message_thread_id` is set only when a thread exists, on BOTH planes (the floor's per-method wrappers and the rich body builder), so a message without a topic lands in the chat's main area rather than in a wrong thread or in none
probes.cmd: test "$(grep -c 'Some(t) => req.message_thread_id(t)' src/channels/telegram/send.rs)" -ge 4 && grep -qF 'if let Some(t) = thread_id {' src/channels/telegram/rich/api.rs

probes.claim: a local document sent through the daemon is stored as a link-form tg://document reference and lands as one bubble
a remote URL written in link syntax stays a hyperlink: no fetch, no unsupported-format trailer
an unbracketed path in prose is claimed by no family and stays inert text
a REMOTE image reference written in embed syntax is fetched and arrives as a photo
a reply carrying documents lands as one bubble, with no degraded HTML copy beside it

the LOCAL photo fixture the live probe feeds the delivery path is a structurally valid PNG: signature, per-chunk CRC32, exact end on IEND, IDAT inflating to h*(1+w*4). `file(1)` is not a validator — it reads IHDR and stops, which is how a truncated fixture certified itself as `valid` and produced #829

the corrupt PNG that triggers a refusal is genuinely broken: a valid PNG signature (all the daemon's `validate_local_image` reads) with a CRC-broken IDAT, so the file IS claimed locally and IS refused by Telegram's processor. A fixture that healed would turn the AC-3 probe into a no-op

the video fixture carries the shape rule 2 detects: `ftyp` as the FIRST box, a non-audio-only brand, and both `moov` and `mdat` inside the file. A renamed text file would satisfy `file(1)` and measure nothing

the oversize fixture is a structurally VALID PNG above the 10 MiB photo ceiling (12.01 MiB), so the floor's size split is measured with a real image rather than a truncated one. Generated by `fixtures/make_oversize.py`, kept out of git
the captioned-image fixture is a structurally valid PNG distinct in bytes from every other fixture, so a caption probe cannot be answered by a file another reference already claimed
the inexpressible-caption fixture is a structurally valid PNG, distinct in bytes, so the caption-drop probe measures the GATE rather than a file that failed for its own reasons
a LOCAL image reference written in embed syntax is attached as a photo; the measured failure is that its bytes are refused and the picture never arrives
the tree that carries every rule above compiles and passes its tests on the CI gate

probes.claim: with no rich path the local image's bytes still ship, as their own detached bubble (the floor), rather than being held back

a LOCAL image referenced in LINK syntax `[label](path)` is still claimed by the image family and arrives as a photo entry — the two markdown forms are equivalent for local targets, which is the property that makes link syntax safe to author

one reply carrying an image, a video and a document produces ONE rich bubble in which each reference is answered by its own kind: the image binds as a photo entry, the video as a video entry, and the document as a link-form `tg://document` reference (ADR §4.2 measures that a document deliberately never rides as an entry - its embed form draws nothing in the client). Not three entries: the document is a reference by design.
probes.claim_revised: 2026-11-14: the original claim demanded three media ENTRIES, which contradicts ADR §4.2. See live-evidence L9.

probes.claim: a document authored in EMBED syntax is demoted to link syntax at send time (`shield_unresolvable_markdown_images`), so it lands tappable instead of drawing nothing — the #827 failure mode cannot be re-authored from a reply
a local MP4 in embed syntax arrives as a `video` media entry (playable), not as a document and not as a dead reference
an expressible caption rides the reference's markdown title and arrives as the media caption, which is the only caption channel the rich plane offers
a caption containing `)` is DROPPED rather than emitted malformed: the image still arrives, merely unnamed, and the reference is not mangled
one file referenced twice in one reply under two spellings (`~/…` and `/root/…`) is delivered ONCE: dedup compares the resolved absolute path
a reply whose media plane contains a file Telegram refuses (`IMAGE_PROCESS_FAILED`) still lands as ONE bubble carrying the healthy entries, instead of downgrading the whole reply to the HTML dialect
a structurally valid 12.01 MiB image is above the `sendPhoto` ceiling, so the floor ships it as a document: it arrives as a file rather than being refused
